author: Mike Helms
text:
What is the concern here? Those numbers are practically the same.

But as any diabetic with common sense knows, a finger stick is still the gold standard and is the ultimate number to use.

Edit to add: With that high a number, you need to get your blood sugar under control. EiBy medication and/exercise.

author: Karen Kennedy
text: This is when we have to ask, "Does it matter?" Your blood sugar is high. Both CGMs tell you in no uncertain terms that what you ate/did earlier is incompatible with your metabolism. If you are someone who needs to know more exact numbers (and some of us do need that), be sure to purchase a glucometer (finger stick) and test it against the lab to "calibrate" it. Because even a glucometer is not the gold standard. Then you can use your standardized glucometer to check each CGM. But remember, when blood sugar is changing rapidly (like this situation), it's not easy to compare blood glucose to interstitial glucose levels.
